newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's business conditions not bad - Keidanren.
newsitem.headline: Japan's business conditions not bad - Keidanren.

text.p: Japan's current business conditions are not reassuring but are not bad, Shoichiro Toyoda, chairman of the powerful business lobby Keidanren, the Federation of Economic Organisations, said on Monday.
"Although there is not much confidence in the economy, I don't think the conditions at the moment are bad," Toyoda told a regular news conference.

Asked about recent weakness in the stock market, Toyoda said he was worried about the price falls, but added that movements in stock prices do not necessarily coincide with those in corporate earnings.
He also said the government should not "fiddle" with the market to support prices.
But in order to revive the economy, Toyoda called for thorough bureaucratic reforms, quick passage of laws to carry out fiscal reforms and measures to promote the real estate market.
On the Tokyo stock market, the key Nikkei average of 225 leading shares soared 815.14 points to end at 18,118.79 on Monday, rebounding from losses of over 2,000 points last week.
